summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

primary_citations.citation_text: New Mexico - NMSA 1978 Chapter 32A, Article 4 (Abuse and Neglect Act: 32A-4-3 duty to report, 32A-4-18 custody hearings, 32A-4-19 adjudicatory hearings), CYFD-published Children's Code compilation (2023 text; 32A-4-3 amended 2025 by SB 42)

New Mexico Statutes Chapter 27 - Public Assistance (public assistance and Medicaid programs; CYFD's child-welfare authority is not in this chapter — it is the Children, Youth and Families Department Act, NMSA 1978 § 9-2A-7(D), and the Children's Code, NMSA 1978 § 32A-1-1, per 8.10.3.3 NMAC)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Children, Youth & Families Department v. Mafin M.
key_cases.holding: Applying the Mathews v. Eldridge factors, the Court held that a mother's procedural due process rights were not violated when the district court terminated her parental rights at a hearing she did not attend, and it reinstated the termination.
key_cases.relevance: The case began when the mother herself called police and asked the State to take custody, and the Court treats that voluntary request as the lawful entry point into the dependency system.
key_cases.quote: because the right to raise one's child is a fundamental right protected by the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, termination proceedings must be conducted in a constitutional manner

key_cases.case_name: In re Guardianship of Ashleigh R.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the trial court had no authority to appoint guardians over a parent's objection absent proof of present unfitness or extraordinary circumstances, and that voluntary relinquishment of custody plus the children's attachment to the grandparents did not supply those circumstances.
key_cases.relevance: It arose from a parent's own voluntary handover of her children to relatives without any agency petition.
key_cases.quote: We hold that Grandparents presented insufficient evidence to prove that Mother was unfit to care for her children at the time of the hearing

reporting_details: In New Mexico every person who knows or has a reasonable suspicion that a child is abused or neglected must report it immediately to a local law enforcement agency, to CYFD (Statewide Central Intake, 1-855-333-7233), or, for an Indian child residing in Indian country, to a tribal law enforcement or social services agency, and failing to report is a misdemeanor (NMSA 1978 § 32A-4-3(A), (F)). A finding that a pregnant woman is using or abusing drugs, made pursuant to an interview, self-report, clinical observation or routine toxicology screen, does not alone form a sufficient basis to report child abuse or neglect, and a volunteer, contractor or staff member of a hospital or freestanding birthing center shall not make a report based solely on that finding; notification of a plan of safe care goes to the health care authority and is not a report of abuse or neglect (NMSA 1978 § 32A-4-3(G)–(I), as amended by Laws 2025, ch. 156).
